cases.description: lesson vector — paraphrased query, semantic dominant

memories.content: When an agent boot fails with a Vault authentication error, the root cause is almost always a stale token. Rotating the token and reprovisioning resolves it within 2 minutes.
Reflection cycles that produce more than 5 new mental models in one pass are usually a sign of too many episodic memories queued. Increase the reflection threshold.

hard_negatives.content: When a database connection fails with an authentication error, the root cause is usually an expired password. Rotating the password and restarting the service resolves it.

query.query: agent fails to start because of authentication problem

cases.description: lesson vector — semantic paraphrase for operational pattern

memories.content: Never lower a coverage floor in CI. If tests are deleted, re-evaluate the floor and document the decision. Silent coverage drops hide regressions.
Always pin security scanner actions to exact tags in CI. Floating @main is a supply-chain risk.

hard_negatives.content: Never lower a performance budget in the frontend build. If components are removed, re-evaluate the budget.

query.query: what we learned about test coverage thresholds

cases.description: lesson vector — semantic paraphrase for security lesson

memories.content: Passing secrets as subprocess arguments exposes them in /proc/<pid>/cmdline. Always use environment variables or file descriptors for secret injection.
Floating Docker image tags in production cause non-deterministic builds. Always pin to a specific digest or version tag.

hard_negatives.content: Passing user input directly to SQL queries causes injection vulnerabilities. Always use parameterised queries.

query.query: how secrets can leak through process metadata

cases.description: lesson vector — semantic paraphrase for async pattern

memories.content: asyncio primitives (Event, Queue, Lock) bind to the running event loop at first use in Python 3.13. Creating them outside a coroutine causes LoopBoundMixin errors in multi-threaded test setups.
Using pytest-asyncio with a background thread for the app server requires all asyncio objects to be created inside the background coroutine.

hard_negatives.content: threading.Event and threading.Lock are safe to create outside coroutines. They are not bound to an event loop.

query.query: problems with event loop and async objects in tests

cases.description: lesson vector — semantic paraphrase for migration pattern

memories.content: Never edit an existing Flyway migration. Flyway validates checksums on startup and will reject a modified migration with a checksum mismatch error, blocking all deployments.
Always add a DEFAULT value when adding a new column to an existing table. Postgres will reject the migration if existing rows cannot satisfy a NOT NULL constraint without a default.

hard_negatives.content: Never edit an existing Liquibase changeset. Liquibase validates checksums and will fail if a changeset is modified after it has been applied.

query.query: why you cannot change a migration after it runs

cases.description: mental model hybrid — full pipeline, related-but-wrong hard negative

memories.content: Agents that accumulate more than 30 episodic memories without a reflection cycle develop context drift — their tool calls become less precise because the LLM context is dominated by raw events rather than synthesised patterns.
Triggered a reflection cycle after 35 episodic memories. Tool call precision improved in the next session.

hard_negatives.content: Agents that accumulate more than 30 org memories without a weekly summary develop knowledge fragmentation — their recall becomes less coherent because the org memory corpus is too large.

query.query: what happens when agents skip reflection for too long

cases.description: mental model hybrid — architectural pattern, paraphrased query

memories.content: The vault.py boundary invariant: no file outside vault.py may call _vault_client directly. This prevents scattered Vault logic and ensures all error handling is centralised.
The tenant_transaction invariant: all tenant-scoped DB writes must go through tenant_transaction() to ensure RLS context is set correctly.

hard_negatives.content: The db.py boundary invariant: no file outside db.py may call asyncpg directly. This prevents scattered connection management.

query.query: rules about accessing the secrets store from application code

cases.description: mental model hybrid — operational pattern, semantic query

memories.content: Boot failures in agent containers almost always trace to one of three root causes: Vault token expired, runtime.json schema mismatch, or missing capability (CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE). Check Loki for the boot_failed.step field first.
Investigated a boot failure. Root cause was a stale Vault token after a Vault restart.

hard_negatives.content: Platform startup failures almost always trace to one of three root causes: database connection refused, LiteLLM gateway unreachable, or missing environment variable. Check the platform logs first.

query.query: how to diagnose why an agent container will not start

cases.description: mental model hybrid — quality pattern, semantic query

memories.content: LLM reranking on recall results with fewer than 2 items adds latency without quality gain. The reranker needs at least 2 candidates to produce a meaningful ordering.
Observed 35-second recall latency spikes on cold-start agents. Root cause was unconditional LLM rerank on single-result sets.

hard_negatives.content: LLM summarisation on memory sets with fewer than 3 items adds cost without quality gain. The summariser needs at least 3 items to produce a meaningful summary.

query.query: when reranking hurts more than it helps

cases.description: mental model hybrid — multi-tenancy pattern, semantic query

memories.content: Any finding that allows Tenant A to read data belonging to Tenant B is automatically Critical severity, regardless of exploit complexity. Tenant isolation is the primary security invariant of the platform.
RLS policies must be enabled on all data tables and disabled on all auth.* tables. The audit_rls.py script enforces this on every PR.

hard_negatives.content: Any finding that allows User A to read data belonging to User B within the same tenant is High severity. User isolation within a tenant is enforced by application-level checks.

query.query: severity of cross-tenant data access vulnerabilities
